title: A Survey of Toxicity Detection and Mitigation Strategies for Multilingual Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying and synthesizing evaluations of toxicity detection and mitigation models across different languages, dialects, code-switched text, and transliterated inputs to identify performance disparities and tokenization brittleness between high-resource and low-resource languages.

Analyzing the cross-cultural transferability of safety alignment pipelines to identify normative misalignments, such as the misclassification of culturally specific expressions, reclaimed slurs, and local conversational norms due to the reliance on English-centric training and preference data.

Examining evaluation frameworks that measure the over-suppression of identity-related language and the marginalization of vulnerable groups caused by automated toxicity filtering, contrastive finetuning, and decoding-time steering techniques.
